subject: history_social
passage: The Khewra Salt Mine in Pakistan's Punjab province is one of the largest salt mines in the world. A popular legend says that the salt was discovered around 326 BCE, when the horses of Alexander the Great's army stopped to rest nearby and were seen licking the rocks.
passage_b: The story of Alexander's horses is charming, but historians doubt that it explains how the salt was found. The salt lies in a range of hills where people had lived for many centuries before Alexander arrived, and the rock salt shows clearly in many places. Local communities, these historians argue, were very likely using it long before any foreign army came.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the legend in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that Alexander's army was the first to make use of the salt
choices.B: By suggesting that local people probably knew of the salt long before Alexander
choices.C: By arguing that the Khewra mine is smaller than it is often said to be
choices.D: By claiming that Alexander's army never traveled through the region

explanation.why: Text 1 reports the legend that Alexander's horses led to the salt's discovery. Text 2 says historians doubt this, since people had lived in the hills "for many centuries before Alexander arrived" and were "very likely using it long before any foreign army came." So Text 2 offers a different, earlier discovery.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 argues that local people were likely using the salt before Alexander's army arrived.
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 says local communities were "very likely using it long before any foreign army came."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 never discusses the size of the mine.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 doubts only that the horses explain the discovery; it does not deny that Alexander's army came to the region.
